subject: Finova - Performance SLOs & Multi-region Routing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs, routing & residency (Finova)

Thanks for the time today, Alice — great conversation. Capturing the notes and next steps from the call so we have a single place to track: 

Summary of Finova requirements (as discussed)
- Latency targets:
  - Short prompts (<=256 tokens): p50 < 40ms, p95 < 150ms
  - Long-form/streaming sessions: p50 < 120ms for initial token, steady-state streaming p95 < 200ms per token
- Throughput & concurrency:
  - Sustained throughput target: ~200 requests/sec across the org during peak
  - Per-tenant concurrency target: ~50 simultaneous sessions (burst to 120 for short windows)
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming required for chat UX (SSE preferred), with a max initial response delay of 200ms
- Regional routing & residency:
  - EU: all request data must remain in EU region (data residency requirement)
  - APAC: low-latency routing to APAC endpoints; target region p95 end-to-end latency <= 200ms
  - US: serve from us-west/us-east as appropriate; failover to secondary region if primary is degraded
- Compliance: SOC2 and audit logs are required for procurement/GPDR attestation

Redwood proposal highlights (high level)
- Multi-region deployment with region-specific control planes to satisfy EU residency
- Regional model replicas + smart routing policy (latency-first with cost fallback)
- KV/prefix caching at the edge to reduce cold-token latency for repeated prompts
- Streaming over SSE/WebSocket with adaptive batching for throughput efficiency

Attachments: network_latency_report.csv (sample RTT matrix from initial ping tests)

Next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with Aditya & Lukas to validate architecture and run a short perf test (30–60 minutes) — proposed week of Mar 16.
2) Send SLO matrix and proposed rollout plan (we'll attach the SLO XLSX).
3) Procurement: we'll work with Tom's team on contract language around residency and SOC2 (Tom/Procurement CC'd).

Would you be available for the deep-dive on Wed 3/17 at 10am PT? If not, toss a couple of slots and we'll align.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs, routing & residency (Finova)

Hi Alice / team — quick tech notes ahead of the deep-dive. High-level approach that meets Marissa's summary and your constraints: 

1) Region pinning & residency
- We support per-account region pinning (can provision a control plane and dedicated compute in eu-west-1). All request payloads, logs, and KV cache can be configured to stay within region; we also support optional on-prem connectors for additional controls.

2) Multi-region routing & latency
- Recommend regional replicas in us-west, eu-central, ap-southeast. Routing policy: latency-first (client probes) with a cost-weighted fallback. We can enforce sticky routing per-user to preserve residency.
- To meet APAC p95 <=200ms we suggest: edge TCP termination in APAC + regional model replica; quantify during perf test.

3) Streaming & SLO definitions
- Streaming via SSE or WebSocket; server emits tokens and we measure token-emit latency (server-side) and end-to-end observed latency (client). Proposed SLOs: token-emit p95 < 200ms (APAC), p95 < 150ms (US/EU) for steady-state. Initial token allowance higher for longer context.

4) Throughput, concurrency, testing
- For 200 rps sustained and 50 concurrent sessions per tenant we'll provision a cluster sized for peak QPS with autoscaling headroom. We'll run a staged perf test:
  - Ramp test (1 hour) up to 1.5x expected peak
  - Steady-state test (30 min) at expected peak
  - Spike test to validate burst handling

5) Data safeguards & compliance
- SOC2 controls: audit logs, key management integrations (KMS), and export controls. We'll provide an evidence package (SOC2 report + logs) for procurement during negotiation.

Attachments: redwood_slo_matrix.xlsx (proposed SLO matrix + acceptance criteria). I'll drop the XLSX to the shared Drive link before the deep-dive.

Technical ask for deep-dive
- Can Finova provide a small representative prompt set (10–20 prompts) and sample traffic profile (qps distribution, session lengths)? That will let us tailor the perf test and sizing.

Looking forward to the call,
Aditya Rao
